findings.title: Unchecked allocation/thread creation can strand startup or crash under resource pressure
findings.trigger: Force failure of slock_new/scond_new/savedState malloc/pipe/sthread_create before the native worker starts, e.g. memory/FD/thread exhaustion.
findings.cause: Thread NULL is not checked, then UI waits forever for running with no worker. Mutex NULL is silently ignored by the real slock_lock guard, so synchronization is absent; scond_wait dereferences lock and condition and can subsequently crash. SavedState NULL is passed to memcpy; condition NULL accepted into instance; pipe failure leaks mutex/condition; null instance releases reservation but does not finish Activity.
findings.effect: ANR or crash while starting; extra resource leaks on pipe failure. This is not evidence of CPU100% and not proven cause of historical g52 incident.
findings.evidence: native-allocation-candidate-receipt.json; exact production android_app_create and onCreate creation tail; six resource faults plus success case
findings.minimalCandidate: Check allocators before use; cleanup own savedState/cond/mutex/pipe on startup failure; returnNULL without wait/join when no worker; release reservation and NativeActivity_finish only on null instance.
findings.candidateTests: Six injected failures return safely with zero allocations/FDs alive and one release/finish; success returns a mocked running handshake with no finish. All other production source bytes preserved. These controlled fixtures do not prove concurrent Android lifecycle behavior.
findings.integrationRisk: Future incorporation needs AndroidNDK compilation, new runtime/engine identities, signed APK entry preservation and all-phone startup/exit/memory-pressure tests; no runtime was published in this audit.

findings.title: Main-thread native lifecycle waits can still stall if core/driver never returns
findings.trigger: Core or GL/audio/save driver remains blocked while UI requests pause/window/destroy; quit wake cannot preempt a stuck driver.
findings.cause: Condition waits and workerjoin have no deadline; destroyed is now reliably published for an ordinary or early return, but cannot be published if worker never returns.
findings.effect: PossibleANR, no evidence of CPU100% from waiting; R138 fixes stale looper exit but does not solve arbitrary driver stalls.
findings.minimalNextStep: Use Android trace of a remaining physical stall. Do not free live native objects or force another thread/process as a timeout workaround. No code change justified by this risk alone.

findings.title: Control polling and background retained sessions have measurable fixed wakeup cost
findings.details: Up to4 hostlinks means16 control ticks/s; RetroArch paused loop20/s; PSX/Dolphin20/s; game owner20s. Terminal gates immediately return and background does not request fresh tickets. Native/barrier correctness constrains timing. No physical CPU/temperature measurement was collected; reducing frequencies without traces could delay reconnect/ACK/READY.
findings.minimalNextStep: Measure only after consistent R138 devices and signed registry; preserve existing frequencies until a specific cost/latency issue is measured.

findings.title: Social event loops depend on server long-poll contract on successful responses
findings.details: Error loops back off/cancel; successful events immediately repoll, relying on server to wait when revision unchanged. Rapid repeated unchanged200 responses or high global revision churn could amplify signed payload parsing/copies. No current server misbehavior/physical CPU surge is proved. v3snapshot separate poll already has1s delay.
findings.minimalNextStep: Verify response elapsed/revision and CPUtrace if a real surge occurs; add no blind sleeps or protocol weakening without such evidence.

findings.title: A JNI TLS key is created per native Activity and has no matching delete/reuse
findings.details: pthread_key_create overwrites the static thread_key for each accepted native launch. Full corresponding runtime C/C++/headers search finds no pthread_key_delete for that private key; unrelated glslang, VCOS and generic rthreads TLS deletion refer to their own keys. android_app_free/onDestroy join the worker but do not delete this key. StationRetroActivity onRetroArchExit/requestHumanExit/finish have no explicit process exit. If the same Android process is retained across launches, keys can accumulate; allocation failure is only logged and launch continues. Actual same-process/library retention and repeated-launch key allocation were not physically measured; no Android key limit/failure count is asserted.
findings.effect: Resource leak and eventual JNI destructor/key setup failure during repeated use; not evidence of CPU 100%.
findings.minimalNextStep: Qualify repeated start/exit in one retained process and error injection. Consider creating a single process-lifetime key once with checked failure, or deleting it only after all users/worker have ended. Do not delete a key while its worker JNI destructor can still use it.
